newsitem.title: PERU: About 30 Japanese nationals still hostage in Lima.
newsitem.headline: About 30 Japanese nationals still hostage in Lima.

text.p: Japanese officials in Lima said on Monday that over 30 Japanese nationals were still captive in the ambassador's residence, including top executives of the Peruvian branches of Japanese companies and some diplomats.

The executives included those of such blue-chip companies such as Mitsubishi Corp and Toyota Motor Corp as well as the host of the ill-fated reception stormed by Marxist guerrillas, Japanese ambassador Morihisa Aoki.
"We don't know why but it is true that (Japanese) employees holding high-ranking posts have not been released," a spokesman for Mitsui Mining and Smelting Co was quoted as saying in Tokyo.
Three of Mitsui Mining's local branch staff were released on Sunday, but others were still inside. The president of Honda Motors Peru, Peruvian national Octavio Mavila, was also released.

About half of the approximately 60 Japanese nationals held were freed with other foreign hostages in Sunday night's release of the 225 men by the Marxist Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA). Most of them were not highly ranked or were unaffiliated with big-name businesses.
Other Japanese citizens also released on Sunday included teachers at the Japanese schools in Peru, and members of the Japan International Cooperation Agency, an aid organisation.
The guerrillas may have decided to release them after taking into account their contribution to the Peruvian people, Japan's Kyodo News Agency reported.
